provenance.method: mapper and verifier agents, a judge ruled; finding confirmed by two skeptics, then by two more after a judge revised it; note corrected after a review of the headline statements; source of nasqret/z-in-q-lean and its dependency at their pins read, not built

evidence: [N] has no general-R form of max(1,h_F(A)) <= max(1,C_cm,Q_R^17) M_S^24: a search for Q^17 finds it only at heightQ heightD. Besides GeometricComparisons, it also appears in the proved ZInQBlueprint.HeightBudget.third_comparison, but only at R = D and S = S_mul, from a von Kaenel bound taken as hypothesis, so the R = D restriction stands. The other parts are as described; [N]'s constants there (+16, 2^23) are better than [M]'s.

Survives: the j identity, h(j) <= 40h+22 (and +16, level-two form) and theta_le (2^23, conditional on Pazuki's inequality as hypothesis) are as described, while the first display is proved only as third_comparison, an arithmetic bound for any real below vonKaenelBudget at S = S_mul, so the clause for general S is missing. One correction: restricting to R = D is not itself a weakening, since D is the least admissible R when max S <= D and Q_R increases with R; the real loss is the fixed S = S_mul (and the von Kanel input in place of the CM/non-CM argument).

third_comparison fixes R = D (heightQ heightD) and S = S_mul and takes the stable-height bound as hypothesis hv; no nasqret declaration uses heightQ at a general R in this comparison, while [M] lines 392-405 allow any S and R >= max(D, max S, 10^12). The other parts (IgusaRatio.quotient, ratHeight_le +22/+16, level-two form, theta_le from Pazuki as hypothesis) are as described, so the weaker finding stands.
